metadata.title: TMUA 2018 · Paper 2
metadata.description: Worked steps, progressive hints and reviewed follow-up questions.

matches.rationale: Both expand or split a radical quotient into fractional powers and then apply the power rule term by term; the candidate asks for the formula instead of its value.
sharedKnowledge: Both expand or split a radical quotient into fractional powers and then apply the power rule term by term; the candidate asks for the formula instead of its value.

matches.rationale: Both simplify a radical denominator to powers, differentiate and substitute a specified positive input.
sharedKnowledge: Both simplify a radical denominator to powers, differentiate and substitute a specified positive input.

matches.rationale: Both select the number of reciprocal-factor choices by equating the total power of x to the requested exponent, then compute the binomial coefficient.
sharedKnowledge: Both select the number of reciprocal-factor choices by equating the total power of x to the requested exponent, then compute the binomial coefficient.

matches.rationale: Both track which selections of terms contribute a targeted power. This candidate combines low-degree contributions from a polynomial product, extending coefficient selection rather than repeating the negative-power equation.
sharedKnowledge: Both track which selections of terms contribute a targeted power. This candidate combines low-degree contributions from a polynomial product, extending coefficient selection rather than repeating the negative-power equation.

matches.rationale: Both recover the combined total from unequal weighted contributions. Here mixture volumes weight ingredient percentages, whereas journey durations weight speeds; the candidate does not test a logical counterexample.
sharedKnowledge: Both recover the combined total from unequal weighted contributions. Here mixture volumes weight ingredient percentages, whereas journey durations weight speeds; the candidate does not test a logical counterexample.

matches.rationale: Both retain both cosine signs after an equation involving a square or modulus, reject impossible levels and count intersections on the stated interval; this candidate finally sums the roots.
sharedKnowledge: Both retain both cosine signs after an equation involving a square or modulus, reject impossible levels and count intersections on the stated interval; this candidate finally sums the roots.

matches.rationale: Both split a squared cosine equation into its two levels, rescale the angular interval and count all permitted branches, with endpoint checks.
sharedKnowledge: Both split a squared cosine equation into its two levels, rescale the angular interval and count all permitted branches, with endpoint checks.

matches.rationale: Both construct an allowed quadrilateral satisfying the stated side or diagonal conditions while violating an unjustified stronger shape property; the candidate distinguishes necessity from sufficiency.
sharedKnowledge: Both construct an allowed quadrilateral satisfying the stated side or diagonal conditions while violating an unjustified stronger shape property; the candidate distinguishes necessity from sufficiency.

matches.rationale: Both test whether perpendicular diagonals or related quadrilateral conditions force a square or stronger symmetry, retaining all premises when constructing a nonsquare example.
sharedKnowledge: Both test whether perpendicular diagonals or related quadrilateral conditions force a square or stronger symmetry, retaining all premises when constructing a nonsquare example.

matches.rationale: Both separate function height from derivative information and construct a polynomial counterexample satisfying an all-input monotonicity premise. The candidate additionally distinguishes first from second derivative ordering.
sharedKnowledge: Both separate function height from derivative information and construct a polynomial counterexample satisfying an all-input monotonicity premise. The candidate additionally distinguishes first from second derivative ordering.

matches.rationale: Both audit an algebraic solution by substituting candidates into the original radical equation and locating a non-equivalent step. The original loses a root by division; this candidate gains one by squaring.
sharedKnowledge: Both audit an algebraic solution by substituting candidates into the original radical equation and locating a non-equivalent step. The original loses a root by division; this candidate gains one by squaring.

matches.rationale: Both identify the first invalid inference in a displayed argument and verify the earlier steps on their domain. The candidate tests an unjustified product inference instead of a zero-divisor cancellation.
sharedKnowledge: Both identify the first invalid inference in a displayed argument and verify the earlier steps on their domain. The candidate tests an unjustified product inference instead of a zero-divisor cancellation.

matches.rationale: Both translate reflections and shifts into identities in an arbitrary function and rename the universally quantified input to compare equivalent conditions.
sharedKnowledge: Both translate reflections and shifts into identities in an arbitrary function and rename the universally quantified input to compare equivalent conditions.

matches.rationale: Both identify the centre of paired inputs in an identity for an arbitrary function. Opposite values around the integration midpoint then give cancellation; this is rotational rather than reflection symmetry.
sharedKnowledge: Both identify the centre of paired inputs in an identity for an arbitrary function. Opposite values around the integration midpoint then give cancellation; this is rotational rather than reflection symmetry.

matches.rationale: Both negate a nested quantified definition one scope at a time while retaining domains and inner dependence; the candidate has a prime-factor sharing condition.
sharedKnowledge: Both negate a nested quantified definition one scope at a time while retaining domains and inner dependence; the candidate has a prime-factor sharing condition.

matches.rationale: Both negate a universal-existential definition while preserving restrictions on the chosen variables; the candidate expresses the negated existence as no divisor from the set.
sharedKnowledge: Both negate a universal-existential definition while preserving restrictions on the chosen variables; the candidate expresses the negated existence as no divisor from the set.

matches.rationale: Both locate the first step that drops the negative possibility when reversing a square, retaining principal-root and trigonometric sign information.
sharedKnowledge: Both locate the first step that drops the negative possibility when reversing a square, retaining principal-root and trigonometric sign information.

matches.rationale: Both audit a trigonometric argument for missing sign or angle cases rather than accepting its final claim. The candidate needs all periodic tangent solutions, not a square-root sign split.
sharedKnowledge: Both audit a trigonometric argument for missing sign or angle cases rather than accepting its final claim. The candidate needs all periodic tangent solutions, not a square-root sign split.

matches.rationale: Both count the possible SSA triangles by comparing the opposite side with the altitude and the given side, then exclude degenerate boundary configurations.
sharedKnowledge: Both count the possible SSA triangles by comparing the opposite side with the altitude and the given side, then exclude degenerate boundary configurations.

matches.rationale: Both differentiate a cubic and compare its two turning heights with a horizontal level to determine when three distinct roots occur.
sharedKnowledge: Both differentiate a cubic and compare its two turning heights with a horizontal level to determine when three distinct roots occur.

matches.rationale: Both compute a cubic maximum and minimum and compare their heights with the required horizontal level, distinguishing a guaranteed root count from a merely possible one.
sharedKnowledge: Both compute a cubic maximum and minimum and compare their heights with the required horizontal level, distinguishing a guaranteed root count from a merely possible one.

matches.rationale: Both use integer AP parameters to test parity assertions and construct allowed finite-sequence counterexamples; one asks about a fixed sum and the other median integrality.
sharedKnowledge: Both use integer AP parameters to test parity assertions and construct allowed finite-sequence counterexamples; one asks about a fixed sum and the other median integrality.

matches.rationale: Both distinguish the odd-list middle entry from the even-list mean of two entries, and use allowed lists to test an alleged necessary parity condition.
sharedKnowledge: Both distinguish the odd-list middle entry from the even-list mean of two entries, and use allowed lists to test an alleged necessary parity condition.

matches.rationale: Both ask whether a product condition forces a condition on at least one factor and require a counterexample retaining the premise. The candidate uses ordinary divisibility, so the supplied awkward-prime theorem is replaced by a simpler prerequisite.
sharedKnowledge: Both ask whether a product condition forces a condition on at least one factor and require a counterexample retaining the premise. The candidate uses ordinary divisibility, so the supplied awkward-prime theorem is replaced by a simpler prerequisite.

matches.rationale: Both test product-to-factor reasoning separately from factor-to-product reasoning; composite divisibility gives a simpler prerequisite for handling summed prime exponents.
sharedKnowledge: Both test product-to-factor reasoning separately from factor-to-product reasoning; composite divisibility gives a simpler prerequisite for handling summed prime exponents.

matches.rationale: Both connect chord position to the sign of the second derivative while distinguishing curvature from slope. One establishes a necessary midpoint condition and the other tests a sufficient trapezium-error condition.
sharedKnowledge: Both connect chord position to the sign of the second derivative while distinguishing curvature from slope. One establishes a necessary midpoint condition and the other tests a sufficient trapezium-error condition.

matches.rationale: Both compare straight chords with a curved graph. The candidate applies that geometry to trapezium error under transformations, while the original expresses a universal midpoint inequality in derivative language.
sharedKnowledge: Both compare straight chords with a curved graph. The candidate applies that geometry to trapezium error under transformations, while the original expresses a universal midpoint inequality in derivative language.

matches.rationale: Both prove universal inequalities by multiplying or dividing only after checking signs and by comparing ordered quantities. The candidate uses negative numbers and reverses inequalities instead of positive exponential factors.
sharedKnowledge: Both prove universal inequalities by multiplying or dividing only after checking signs and by comparing ordered quantities. The candidate uses negative numbers and reverses inequalities instead of positive exponential factors.

matches.rationale: Both order exponents and use a common exponential base greater than one to preserve that order. The candidate then transfers the pointwise comparison to integrals, extending this prerequisite.
sharedKnowledge: Both order exponents and use a common exponential base greater than one to preserve that order. The candidate then transfers the pointwise comparison to integrals, extending this prerequisite.
